summary: RETEST of the Provider Ledger fixes from iteration 13. Backend: 59/59 pytest passed. This covers 46 tests in test_provider_ledger.py, where I updated the Xenon assertions to 1 merged patient (they still said 2), plus 13 new tests in test_ledger_fixes_iter14.py. Verified fixes: (1) Race: 6 concurrent POST /invoices for the same provider and month gave exactly one 200 and five 400s, with 1 active invoice in the DB. The unique partial index one_active_invoice_per_month (active=true) exists, and void then re-invoice works. (2) Xenon's PENDING_HOSPITAL consultations have billable=false, patient total_amount is 0, and month_auto_amount/month_billable are 0 for 2026-08 and 2026-10. POST invoice for Xenon 2026-10 returns 400 'Nothing billable'. (3) Re-reviewing an approved or rejected entry returns 400. (4) Deleting a promotion twice returns 400. (5) GST: the GSTIN code wins over the state text (GSTIN 27 with state Karnataka → CGST/SGST, place_of_supply 'Maharashtra (27)'). With no GSTIN, the state name decides: Karnataka → IGST 'Karnataka (29)', Maharashtra → CGST. The PDF renders. (6) The manual invoice line patient is filled in (not '—'). UI (Playwright, desktop): clicking a non-name cell of a ledger table row opens the provider page. Xenon shows 1 patient card (Siddharth Gupta, 2 services) with '· not yet billable' on both rows and 'first visit 2026-08-21' as a date. billing-state and settings-state are SELECTs with 37 options. invoice-sac is prefilled with 998599 on first render. The provider console /provider/ledger loads its Patients and Invoices tabs. There were no page errors. All probe data was cleaned up.

minor.issue: The invoice-number counter (ledger_counters find_one_and_update $inc) runs BEFORE insert_one. Requests that lose the race, or that hit DuplicateKeyError, still use up a number. Observed: inv-2025-11 counter = 6 when only 3 invoices were created. GST rules expect consecutive invoice serials. Fix: allocate the number only after a successful insert (insert with a placeholder number, then set it), or roll back by reserving through the active-invoice claim.

The merged patient key (pkey) is the patient_id of the EARLIEST-dated service sharing that phone. Manual services store body.patient_id = pkey at creation time. If an earlier-dated booking under another patient_id later appears for the same phone, or for entries saved before this fix with the other id, the canonical pkey changes. provider_detail then skips the manual entry (patients.get(k) is None): it is hidden from admin and provider, but create_invoice still bills it. Fix: map manual m['patient_id'] through an alias map {any patient_id/phone → pkey}, or store patient_phone and match on it.
A PAID invoice can be voided, which unlocks its items for re-billing, with no audit reason. Consider blocking it or requiring a reason (credit note).

action_items: LOW: Allocate the invoice serial only after the insert succeeds, so there are no gaps in GST invoice numbering.
MEDIUM: Resolve manual-service patient_id through the phone-merge alias map in provider_detail, so entries never become hidden but billable when the canonical pkey changes.
LOW: Block, or audit with a reason, the voiding of PAID invoices.
critical_code_review_comments: ledger.py is 842 lines, above the 700-line guideline. Split render_invoice_html and the invoice routes into ledger_invoice.py.
@r.on_event('startup') on an APIRouter is deprecated in recent FastAPI. Verify it actually fires (the index exists now) or move it to the app lifespan.
The create_invoice pre-check find_one uses status != void, but the index uses active=true. These are consistent today because void sets active=false. Keep both in sync if new statuses are added.
